title: Security Advisory – Node.js Critical Security Patch: Addressing Node2Shell and eMudhra CA Compromise
content_md: Date: November 2, 2026 Affected Versions and Technologies: Node.js: Vulnerable versions across the 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x release lines, as well as affected end-of-life releases. TLS/SSL and X.509: Certificate validation, hostname verification, and certificate-chain trust mechanisms. DNS and c-ares: Node.js DNS APIs and the underlying c-ares library. Brotli (node:zlib): Brotli decompression functionality affected by Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497). Other Brotli-dependent software: Applications and runtimes incorporating vulnerable Brotli implementations. Summary In October 2026, the Node.js project released security updates for its 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x release lines, fixing a total of 10 vulnerabilities: one rated Critical, three High, three Medium, and three Low in severity . The highest severity issue fixed in this release [1] is Critical [5] with CVSS(v4.0) score of 9.2 for CVE-2026-111497(Node2Shell). Other notable vulnerabilities addressed in this security release include CVE-2026-105482 (CVSS v3.0: 7.2), CVE-2026-105483 (CVSS v3.0: 7.4), and CVE-2026-106069 (CVSS v3.0: 7.4), all classified as High severity [6][7][8]. eMudhra CA compromise: This is a separate certificate authority incident, node.js upd
